entry.summary: Among many programming languages, the venerable Lisp has always been a unique presence, a uniqueness often summarized as “Lisp is a programmable programming language.” This means Lisp has powerful metaprogramming capabilities, allowing programmers to freely create new syntactic abstractions. Lisp provides metaprogramming via macros, which are essentially code generators embedded in the language. Beyond Lisp, modern languages like Scala and Rust also offer macro designs, but macros are generally seen as complex, low-level technologies and rarely make it into the average programmer’s toolbox. entry.title: XDSL: General-Purpose Domain-Specific Language Design
entry.summary: The Nop platform offers a language-oriented programming paradigm: when solving problems, we tend to first design a Domain-Specific Language (DSL), and then use that DSL to describe business logic. The Nop platform greatly simplifies the process of creating custom DSLs. The value of a DSL lies in distilling domain-specific logical relationships and defining atomic semantic concepts unique to that domain. The concrete syntax is not the key. After code is parsed by a Lexer and Parser, it yields an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST), and all program semantics are, in principle, carried by the AST. Both XML and JSON are tree structures and can directly represent an AST, thus completely avoiding the need to implement a special Lexer and Parser.
